limitations: 364 of 906 model calls failed. 53 calls PER AGENT failed with 'You've hit your session limit', so the extraction is truncated, not merely lossy.
63 of 149 studies (42%) had at least one partial agent failure.

S5 failed 75 of 169 attempts (44%). S5 supplies the direction label AND the effect size, and a missing S5 removes that study's NULL claims -- measured earlier in this project, S5 failures bias a score UPWARD because they hide nulls. The scores in this run are therefore optimistic by an unknown amount and must not be read as the effect of SCORING_MODEL v8.
S3 failed 65 of 159 attempts (41%), so population and eligibility facts are missing for many studies and invariant 7's refusals could not fire.

The session limit was exhausted by two large analysis workflows run immediately beforehand. CLAUDE.md warns against exactly this: concurrent subagent work draws on the same subscription session limit as a production extraction.
This is the FIRST run under v1.17, so it is also the first that could activate the effect-size path at all -- which makes a clean re-run the only way to measure what v8 does.
20260811_174604_creatine_creatine-monohy.note: Invalid: truncated by the subscription session limit mid-extraction. Superseded by a clean re-run; do not quote any score from it.

limitations: First CLEAN run under SCORING_MODEL v8 and PROMPT_VERSION v1.17: 149 of 150 studies usable, 5 partial agent failures, ZERO session-limit failures.

The effect-size path activated on only 10% of mapped claims, so the score is still mostly vote-counted. Isolated on this same corpus (measured path off vs on), v8 moves muscle_strength +1 and lean_body_mass +1 and nothing else.

The v7 -> v8 score movement is NOT attributable to the scoring model. It is dominated by the extraction changes across PROMPT_VERSION v1.14 -> v1.17 (numbers on nulls, between-arm contrast, claim-splitting churn).
Anchor bands remain uncited judgement for 20 of 21 range anchors, so a pass or fail against them is not yet meaningful.
20260812_062929_creatine_creatine-monohy.note: First clean v8/v1.17 run. Usable as a baseline for the next comparison; not a validated score.

limitations: First run under PROMPT_VERSION v1.18. 149 of 150 studies usable, 12 partial agent failures, 128 of 996 calls failed (none on the session limit).
v1.18 fixed what it targeted: the 'large magnitude but favours neither arm' contradiction fell from 17% of mapped claims to 6%, and effect-size coverage rose from 10% to 16%.

The effect-size scoring model's own contribution remains ~2 points. When the numbers are finally read instead of the labels, they say roughly what the labels said: this corpus's measured per-trial effects on creatine really are small.

STABILITY IS THE BINDING PROBLEM, not the formula. Between the v1.17 and v1.18 runs -- same 149 studies, same scoring model, one field's WORDING changed -- scores moved 23 points in total absolute terms, including lean_body_mass -1 -> +14, while study counts per ECU shifted (lean_body_mass 14 -> 12, muscle_power 30 -> 26). Run-to-run extraction variance currently exceeds the deliberate model change by an order of magnitude.
Consequence: anchor calibration is PREMATURE. A band cannot be fitted to a number that moves 15 points when one prompt field is reworded.
20260812_072850_creatine_creatine-monohy.note: v1.18 run. Use for the coverage measurement, not as a stable score. Extraction stability must be established before any band is calibrated.
